newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 18.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Microsoft reported an 85 percent profit increase in the most recent quarter, far ahead of analyst expectations.

* University of Michigan economist Edward Gramlich was seen as one of President Clinton's likely nominees for one of two open seats on the Federal Reserve Board. The other candidate's identity was not disclosed.
* Norman Augustine, chairman of Lockheed Martin, has told the company's board he planned to step down from the position by year-end, according to people close to the matter.
* The Big Three U.S. automakers, concerned by the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen, are voicing more complaints to the Clinton administration.
* In February, the U.S. trade gap narrowed to $10.4 billion from $12.67 billion, with exports buoyed by civilian-aircraft sales.
* Companies are refinancing debt after the Fed's rate hike last month and in expectation of more rate increases.
* Lead tax writers in Congress joined the administration to try and close a tax loophole companies use to sell units without paying taxes.
* Amid signs Oracle's Lawrence Ellison is considering a takeover bid, Apple Computer took steps to ward off a hostile bidder.
* The U.S. attorney in Boston filed a civil complaint against Sears charging unfair credit-card collection actions.
* Archer Daniels Midland's Dwayne Andreas is turning over the CEO job to his nephew but will remain chairman.
* Dean Buntrock, founder of WMX, says he is ready to hand over management responsibilities to attract a CEO.
* Bell Atlantic's quarterly net income fell 15 percent after a charge.
* Quarterly profits at Bank of Boston and Bankers Trust were better than expected.
* Tobacco talks over a regarding a settlement of industry disputes came about as the reasons motivating participants converged. Talks are expected to reconvene Sunday.
* Silicon Graphics reported an 80 percent decline in quarterly profits, short of expectations.
* Heard on the Street: With cellular phone pioneer Craig McCaw boosting his stake in Nextel Communications, should other investors start dialing in as well?

* Credit markets: Lukoil, one of Russia's largest companies, today will become the first corporation to sell bonds to international investors, a transaction that could pave the way for more such deals in years to come.
